messages:
maya: heads up — seeing repeated powercap events on rack12 (PDU-A) starting ~08:04 UTC, GPUs throttle to 70% and tenant 'deepsearch' p50 jumps from 40ms -> 260ms. logs show coil-temp spikes + nvml throttles.
ron: ugh. does cloud telemetry also show PKG power capping or is it just host-level?
anika: system-events from rack12: 
```
2026-03-15T08:03:55Z PDU-A: limit set 250W -> 190W
2026-03-15T08:04:02Z node-gpu-12a nvml: SM_CLOCK_LIMITED
2026-03-15T08:04:07Z tenant-deepsearch req-latency p50 260ms
```
maya: it's the PDU governor; looks like a cooling hysteresis + datacenter power budget kicking in for that rack.
dave: any correlation with recent warm-pool prefill jobs? we prefilled a large quantize job earlier to that rack. could be noisy neighbor + thermal.
ron: how many deepsearch pods are pinned to the rack? we recently allowed fractional dedicated slices.
anika: currently 6 deepsearch slices (48GB each) + 2 large warmpool prefetches. that's close to max for those hosts.
maya: proposal: soft isolate by temporarily moving warm-pool prefetches off rack12 and migrating 2 deepsearch slices to eu2-edge pool (preemptible). cost tradeoff but reduces thermal density.
dave: alternative: dynamic MIG split on the two most-loaded hosts to 2x20G + 1x8G so warmpool can be throttled without evicting deepsearch. has anyone tested live MIG bubble on that kernel version?
ron: we did a canary last month; MIG re-partitioning had ~5-8s disruption for existing KV caches but restored. worth it if latency win > 150ms per request.
anika: +1 for quick MIG split + migrate prefetch. steps: 1) cordon node, 2) snapshot KVcache, 3) run MIG tool, 4) uncordon. I can run.
maya: sounds good. timeline? deepsearch SLOs are degraded now. ops-bot: scheduled migration window in 15m if ops-approved.
dave: cost-wise, migrating to eu2-edge preemptible will bloat egress and inter-region copy. estimate ~3TB of model shards, that's non-trivial. prefer MIG split first.
ron: agree. Also let's tweak routing: route deepsearch traffic away from hosts with powercap indicator by marking nodes with label `powercap=true` and our allocator will avoid them for new allocations. quick patch:
```yaml
nodeSelector: 
  matchExpressions:
    - key: powercap
      operator: NotIn
      values: ["true"]
```
maya: I'll push that label and trigger a rebalancer check. anika, can you run the MIG split on node-gpu-12a and node-gpu-12b?
anika: running now — will message back with output.
sre-bot: ALERT: thermal governor engaged on rack12: PDU-A limit lowered to 190W. incident created INC-2026-0315-33.
(3 minutes pass)
anika: MIG tool output: node-gpu-12a -> split into [1x24G,1x8G], node-gpu-12b -> split into [2x16G]. disruption: KV cache miss spike ~6s, no pod evictions.
maya: checking metrics — deepsearch p50 back to 48ms on affected hosts. heatmaps show per-GPU power draw dropped ~12%. good.
dave: nice. let's keep `powercap=true` label setting for the next 30m and schedule a follow-up: add a soft-prewarm affinity so future warmpool prefetches avoid racks with recent powercap events for 1h.
ron: can we add a cost counterfactual in the follow-up? MIG splits increase scheduling fragmentation and might raise unit-cost by ~4% depending on bin packing. need to track.
anika: noted. I'll close INC-2026-0315-33 with postmortem: root cause PDU governor + high thermal density from warmpool prefill. mitigation: MIG split + routing label + avoid-prefill policy.
maya: thanks all. follow-up tasks: @dave add avoid-prefill flag to prefill job spec, @ron add allocator rule for `powercap` label, @anika attach PM with numbers. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: actioned tasks: created ticket OPS-4523 (avoid-prefill) and infra-task INFRA-908 (allocator rule).
dave: for longer term, ops we should consider thermal-aware scheduler that factors PDU headroom and recent powercap history into placement cost. low-effort probe: add ExponentialMovingAverage(PowercapEvents) to node score.
ron: agree — would save us from repeated thermal shuffles.
maya: closing thread — will monitor rack12 for 2h and revert labels after stable.
